How to Fix Blank Pages When Printing in Thunderbird

1. Check Print Preview First Before wasting paper, always go to File > Print Preview. If the preview shows blank pages, the issue is how Thunderbird is translating the email. If the preview looks normal but the physical page is blank, it's a printer driver communication error.

2. Switch to Simple HTML (Quickest Fix) Many modern emails use complex coding that breaks Thunderbird's pagination engine. Open the email, click View > Message Body As, and switch it to Simple HTML (or Plain Text). Whizz-Tech Try printing again. This strips away heavy graphics and code that often trigger blank pages. Whizz-Tech

3. Clear Saved Print Settings Sometimes corrupted print configurations get stuck in your profile. Go to Help > Troubleshooting Information. support.mozilla.org Look for the Clear saved print settings button and click it, then restart Thunderbird.

4. Test in Troubleshoot Mode If an add-on or theme is breaking your print layout: Go to Help > Troubleshoot Mode... and click Restart. Try printing the email again. If it works, an extension or theme is causing the conflict. Whizz-Tech

5. The Reliable Workaround If you are in a rush and need the printout immediately, the workaround mentioned in your original text is spot-on: Copy the email text, paste it into Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice, and print from there.

  7. start thunderbird

  9. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  10. exit thunderbird
  11. this should also show profile contents. delete everthing there

Hello there



To make it easier for you to reset your Thunderbird software or printer yourself, I have located a guide to help you get started with your equipment right away.



This issue is usually caused by an outdated or corrupted component in Thunderbird. We will resolve this together by following the steps below.


Step 1: Close ThunderbirdCompletely close the Thunderbird program (click the X in the top right corner).


Step 2: Open the profile folder (instantly)On your keyboard, press the Windows key (the flag icon in the bottom left) and the letter R at the same time.

A small window named Run will open in the bottom-left corner of your screen.

Type the following text exactly into that window: %appdata%\Thunderbird\Profiles click OK. Your computer will now open the correct folder directly.


Step 3: Open the profile folder and delete the settingsYou will likely see one folder with a name consisting of letters and numbers (for example, settings.default). Double-click this folder to open it.

Look for the file named PrintSettings.json (or printsheets.sqlite) in the list.Right-click this file and select Delete (or click the trash can icon). Don't worry: Thunderbird will automatically recreate a fresh, clean version of this file.


Step 4: Testing restart Thunderbird and check if you can print now.


Is it still not working? Open the document directly in your PDF program (such as Adobe Reader) and try printing it from there.
